text:
The Avalanche's season changed on Nov. 21, when Nathan MacKinnon was reevaluated and ruled out for 12 weeks with a lower-body injury. Cale Makar went on injured reserve at the same time, expected back in about two weeks. Colorado lost its two best players in one stretch, and the question for the next three months is simple: can they stay near the top of the Central without them?

The early answer is yes. They are 14-7-3 with 31 points and 6-2-2 in their last 10. Brock Nelson has stepped into the top center job, a role he knows from his years with the Islanders, and his line with Nazem Kadri and Gabriel Landeskog has 57% of the expected goals in a small sample. Mackenzie Blackwood is at .950 over his last five starts, saving 5.3 goals above expected, and Scott Wedgewood shut out Anaheim.

What MacKinnon took with him is real. His line with Artturi Lehkonen and Martin Necas outscored teams 20-10 at 5v5. The team has also finished almost 13 goals above its chances, which is hard to keep up without the league's best shooters. The power play, as Sportsnet's Eric Engels noted, has gone from one of the league's worst last season to a strength (0.81 expected goals a game).

Landeskog's hit on Kaiden Guhle in Montreal made noise too. Our numbers still put Colorado at 97% to make the playoffs. What to watch: Makar's return.
headline: Life without MacKinnon starts now
